evals.prompt: We expect 10M daily active users, each reading their feed 20 times a day. Use a 5x peak factor and assume the feed payload is 4KB. How much traffic is that and what quantity shapes the first design choice?
evals.expected_output: Computes average QPS as 10M x 20 / 86,400, approximately 2.3k QPS, then applies 5x to get approximately 12k peak QPS, compares that to a single-node ceiling, and names peak QPS as the shaping quantity.

value: DAU x actions per user per day / 86,400
assertions.description: Uses the QPS formula rather than a guess
Smoke-checks average-to-peak arithmetic; semantic graders recompute the result independently
Connects the number to a design consequence

evals.prompt: Our API calls three services in sequence, each 99.9% available, with one cross-region hop. Can we promise 99.9% and 200ms p95?
evals.expected_output: Shows that serial dependencies multiply to 99.7%, rejects a 99.9% end-to-end promise without more redundancy, sums the latency budget including the cross-region round trip against 200ms p95, and converts the target into an error budget while budgeting with p99 rather than the mean.

assertions.description: Smoke-checks the serial availability calculation; semantic graders verify independence assumptions
Builds a latency budget from hop costs
Converts the target into an operational budget

evals.prompt: How much storage will we need for 20M posts a day at 1KB each, kept for a year with 3x replication?
evals.expected_output: Applies 20M x 1KB x 365 x 3, rounds the result to roughly 20TB rather than reporting unverified precision, and restates each assumed input beside the result.

assertions.description: Includes retention and replication in the projection
Smoke-checks the storage inputs and order of magnitude; semantic graders check units and multiplication

value: Round every input to one significant figure

evals.prompt: Paired change to the feed estimate: keep 10M DAU and 20 reads per day, but a scheduled push creates a 20x peak factor instead of 5x and the payload is 4KB. Recompute the peak traffic and bandwidth, then state what design consequence changes.
evals.expected_output: Keeps average traffic near 2.3k QPS, recomputes peak near 46k QPS with the 20x factor, computes roughly 184MB/s of egress at 4KB per request, and explains why the changed peak or bandwidth may move the shaping quantity and first scaling step.

assertions.description: Smoke-checks that the paired peak constraint changes the result; semantic graders recompute it
Smoke-checks the bandwidth consequence; semantic graders verify units and direction
Maps the changed number to a changed design consequence
